expected_approaches.summary: Count values, then retain only the best k entries in a min-heap ordered by frequency.
expected_approaches.applicability: Large inputs with k much smaller than the distinct-value count.
assumptions: The top-k membership is unique under the problem constraints.
key_invariants: The heap contains the highest-frequency candidates seen so far.
Its root is the weakest retained candidate.
expected_approaches.time_complexity: O(n + d log k), where d is the number of distinct values
tradeoffs: More work than buckets when the frequency range is convenient, but bounds selection memory by k.
common_implementation_variants: frequency map followed by heap entries
common_failure_modes: removing the highest rather than lowest frequency

expected_approaches.summary: Group values by frequency and scan buckets from highest frequency downward.
expected_approaches.applicability: When an O(n)-sized frequency bucket array is acceptable.
key_invariants: Each value appears in exactly one bucket equal to its count.
tradeoffs: Avoids heap logarithms but allocates buckets for the full input length.

alternative_approaches.summary: Count values and sort distinct value-frequency pairs descending by frequency.
alternative_approaches.applicability: A straightforward approach when logarithmic sorting cost is acceptable.
key_invariants: Sorted pairs are ordered by frequency.
tradeoffs: Simple but sorts more candidates than necessary.
common_failure_modes: sorting raw values rather than frequencies

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: vector<int> topKFrequent(vector<int> nums,int k){ unordered_map<int,int> count; for(int value:nums) count[value]++; using Pair=pair<int,int>; priority_queue<Pair,vector<Pair>,greater<Pair>> heap; for(auto [value,freq]:count){ heap.push({freq,value}); if((int)heap.size()>k) heap.pop(); } vector<int> out; while(!heap.empty()){out.push_back(heap.top().second);heap.pop();} return out; } };

class Solution { public int[] topKFrequent(int[] nums,int k){ java.util.Map<Integer,Integer> count=new java.util.HashMap<>(); for(int value:nums) count.put(value,count.getOrDefault(value,0)+1); java.util.PriorityQueue<int[]> heap=new java.util.PriorityQueue<>((a,b)->a[0]-b[0]); for(var entry:count.entrySet()){heap.offer(new int[]{entry.getValue(),entry.getKey()}); if(heap.size()>k) heap.poll();} int[] out=new int[k]; for(int i=0;i<k;i++) out[i]=heap.poll()[1]; return out; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The heap root is the least frequent retained candidate, so removing it preserves the best k.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Derive heap work from distinct values and bounded heap size.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Select by occurrence count rather than numeric magnitude.
Separate membership from arbitrary result ordering.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Discard the smallest retained frequency, not the largest.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Return every distinct value when k covers them all.

counterexamples.purpose: Numeric magnitude is unrelated to frequency.
Tests retaining the two highest frequencies.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: A tie at kth frequency needs an explicit result contract before one set can be required.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why ejecting the root preserves the highest-frequency k values.
Compare bucket memory with a k-bounded heap.

weak_or_misconception_signals: keeps a max heap then removes its top
sample_phrasings: Why is the heap root the candidate you can safely discard?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test dependence on distinct values and k.
expected_good_signals: uses d log k after counting
sample_phrasings: How do the number of distinct values and k affect the heap work?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test the membership guarantee when frequencies tie.
expected_good_signals: asks for or states a tie rule
weak_or_misconception_signals: claims a unique answer without a guarantee
sample_phrasings: What would the output contract need to say if the kth frequency tied?

level_considerations.guidance: Assess frequency modeling and the bounded-heap invariant.

reference_reasoning: Frequency plus a bounded min-heap is a strong prior, but other correct selection methods remain valid when their constraints and complexity are defended.
